description:
Discovered while completing fz-f98.3. Distinct from the capture-layout invariant (f98.3) and the native-boundary fragmentation: this is an accumulator/return-threading defect specific to reduce/2 (the reduce_first sentinel path) over a non-List Enumerable.

Repro (with f98.3 capture fix; reduce/2 transport now settles): `Enum.reduce(1..3, fn (x, acc) -> x * acc end)` and `Enum.reduce(1..7//2, ...)` panic at runtime:
  fz panic: "Enum.EmptyError"
The fold returns its initial {:cont, :first} accumulator unadvanced -> reduce_first_acc/reduce_first_finish raises EmptyError as if the collection were empty. Controls:
- List reduce/2 WORKS: Enum.reduce([1,3,5,7], fn (x,acc) -> x*acc end) = 105.
- Range reduce/3 WORKS: Enum.reduce(1..7//2, 0, fn (x,acc) -> x+acc end) = 16.
So the defect is the intersection (reduce/2 reduce_first sentinel) x (Range/non-List Enumerable). The `:first | {:acc, b}` accumulator union is threaded through Enumerable.reduce -> Range.reduce; on the non-List path the inner lambda's {:cont, {:acc, _}} result is not delivered back as the next accumulator (likely a return/acc boundary repr mismatch for the sum-typed accumulator across the protocol-dispatched reduce boundary). Blocks fz_f98_range_reduce2 (bfh.2) run/interp/build.
title: Enum.reduce/2 over Range raises Enum.EmptyError: :first|{:acc} accumulator does not thread through the shared bridge over non-List Enumerables
